gate.reason: Proposes Dynamic Tanh, an element-wise operation that replaces normalization layers in Transformers, which is a buildable architectural component.
gate.evidence: as a drop-in replacement for normalization layers in Transformers

mechanism_scan.where: llm extraction, verified quote, Sec. Dynamic Tanh (DyT)
llm extraction, verified quote, Sec. Initialization of alpha for LLMs
mechanism_scan.evidence: initializing $\alpha$ with higher values for DyT layers in attention blocks and lower values for DyT layers in other locations (i.e., within FFN blocks or before the final linear projection) improves performance.

mechanism_scan.where: llm extraction, verified quote, Appendix A, Large Language Models
mechanism_scan.evidence: we introduce an additional learnable scalar parameter immediately after the embedding layer, before any Transformer blocks.

spec.name: arxiv_2503_10622
report: norm = expr:tanh((a*x)) (new op dyt_attn, replaces RMSNorm in attention block; verified quote (Sec. Dynamic Tanh (DyT)): “\mathrm{DyT}(\vx) = \bm{\gamma} * \tanh(\alpha \vx) + \bm{\beta}”); parses in the IR grammar (spec/tools/ir_expr.py), finite in f32 on [-20, 20]; mtstudio checks its gradient against finite differences before training

norm_inputs = ["row", {"kind": "scalar", "init": 0.8, "init_ffn": 0.2, "init_final": 0.2}]: the expr's inputs in order; learned: a (scalar, init 0.8: stated ('LLaMA 7B & 4096 & 32 & 0.8/0.2'); ffn 0.2, final 0.2)

norm: the paper's ((tanh((a*x))*g)+b) is core*g + a over the row expression with its learned per-channel g, b; flex computes expr(...) * gain + bias, both learned per feature (init 1, 0): the same form
new op dyt_other: the norm dyt_attn's expression at the ffn, final norm(s) of the block graph, with its own inits (flex norm_inputs init_<place>)

embed = expr:(x*a) (new op embed_scale, replaces none (added after embedding); verified quote (Appendix A, Large Language Models): “we introduce an additional learnable scalar parameter immediately after the embedding layer, before any Transformer bloc”); parses in the IR grammar (spec/tools/ir_expr.py), finite in f32 on [-20, 20]; mtstudio checks its gradient against finite differences before training
embed_inputs = ["row", {"kind": "scalar", "init": 8.0}]: the expr's inputs in order; learned: a (scalar, init 8: stated as sqrt(d_model): 8 at this run's d = 64)
activation = swiglu (by the operator, --assert; paper: swiglu)
positional = rope (inherited: “In our implementation of LLaMA models~\citep{touvron2023llama, touvron2023llama2, dubey2024llama} with DyT, we introduce”)

residual = residual: not stated by the paper (the extraction marks it inherited, unverified: inherited from llama, whose curated entry has no residual); a highway or plain stream would be a stated departure

attention = exact: not stated by the paper (the extraction marks it inherited, unverified: inherited from llama, whose curated entry has no attention); windowed, linear or sparse attention would be a stated departure
embed = expr:(x*a) on the embed output, before the first block (parity::FlexConfig embed_expr)
position = rope on the flex family (the paper's other flavours are not the llama block's): every head rotated, interleaved pairs, theta 10000, as the llama block and the IR rope node
d=64 layers=2 heads=4 T=64 chosen for this run (paper: {'d_model': 4096, 'n_layers': 32}); the mechanism is the paper's

sft_fit.rule: len(prompt) + len(completion) + 1 end token <= T + 1 (mtstudio load_sft), file order
